checks: Verified that the full-menu revision and its revised three-fiber dependency change only their statements to require ε>0. Their proof hashes match the originals. From 0<ε and ε^d<ρ_d<1, the endpoint A⊂T is compact convex with volume a and 0<ε<1. The accepted binary-core fact with (q,v,V)=(0,1,1) applies and gives the exact integer fibers, unique deepest point (0,g), and Q=Γ+a.

Restrict an attaining ambient cap to z=t1. The measured fibers in that slice occur at t=−1,0,1, with bodies A,T,T when A⊂T. If the restriction is the entire slice it has mass 2+a>Q. Otherwise the cap includes the middle centroid and the three-fiber depth bound gives mass at least Q. Hence equality holds on the slice and every cube base outside the diagonal has zero trace volume.

Checked the equality mechanism in the revised three-fiber menu 055251c2fee2891d. A pure base normal costs at least 1+a. A nonzero continuous normal with interior slack loses positive middle mass on moving its boundary through g. For a through-point cap, R(u)<a implies f(u)+R(u)≥Γ+ρ_d>Q, while R(u)≥a forces f(u)=Γ and a canonical positive direction. In that direction, a tilt L<b−min_A λ_i gives right threshold less than 2b and right volume at least (1−2b)^d≥ρ_d>a. Otherwise the left trace is full and zero right volume is equivalent to L≥1−b. This checks the invoked boundary and canonical-normal conclusion, assuming containment.

The diagonal restriction has the original continuous normal, so its canonical form and through-centroid boundary lift to λ_i(x)+β·z≥b. Since n≥2, each unit vector is off the diagonal. Zero trace volume there is equivalent to b−β_j≥1, giving every coordinate constraint. Conversely for a nonzero cube vertex with r ones the threshold is at least b+r(1−b)≥1. At v_− the threshold is at most b−n(1−b)<0 and hence includes A for positive ε. At threshold one the nonzero cube trace is a single vertex of zero volume.

The critical caps have the same fiberwise volumes as the original cap of their own barycentric direction. Adding a cap leaves all obstacle minima unchanged. Replacing the source cap of the same direction preserves the actual setwise cover since the base-0 trace is identical, the endpoint remains fully covered, and the nonzero bases retain their own covering families. Thus the optimizer and the specified multipliers, and therefore the normalized row and its residual roots (0,c,1,…,1), persist.
The general row gap equals [n−(n+1)c]/(n+2)>0, and Q−ΓM/k=a(1−Γ/2^n)>0 tends to zero with a. For n=3d, Bernoulli gives (n/(n+1))^d>1−d/(n+1)>2/3, whereas Γ>1/3 from (1+1/d)^d<e<3.

Independently checked the planar positive example using integer and rational arithmetic. The triangle has area one, c²=5/9 and c<3/4 by 80<81. The profile check is (609/200)^2=370881/40000<10. The cube has eight parity classes and the endpoint repeats one. Q=409/900, M=801/100, M/k=801/800, raw excess=17/1800 and the objective 9c²=5. The original row gives five weights 1/5, and the gap (9−4√5)/15 is positive by 80<81. The barycentric functions and δ_w are rational affine functions for this T.

Rechecked both recorded raw source digests and locators. The original source c323819a201d7580 §§1, 4–7 supplies the depth setup, complete cap menu, row and exact rational example, and bb78a1a25bcd2390 §2 supplies the diagonal equality argument. The revised positive dilation assumption makes explicit the containment used by those arguments.

issues.defect: The condition 0<a=ε^d<ρ_d permits negative ε in even dimensions. For the displayed d=2,n=3 triangle take ε=−1/10. The base-0 fiber contains the midpoint with continuous coordinate (−1/20,0) of (v_−,(−1/10,0)) and (1,(0,0)). It also contains T. The added triangle with vertices (−1/20,0),(0,0),(0,2) has area 1/20 and is outside the interior of T. Every nonzero cube base has a coordinate one, which precludes any v_− weight, so the other seven cube fibers still have area one. Writing S=|C_0|≥21/20, the actual M=S+7+1/100 exceeds 2^n+a. Also S>M/8 since S>701/700, contradicting nonheaviness. The first paragraph cannot infer A⊂T or invoke either the accepted contained-endpoint theorem or the finite draft.
